title: Module 24: Replication, Sharding & Partitioning Strategies (All Chapters)
description: Comprehensive module-level assessment covering all chapters of Module 24: Replication, Sharding & Partitioning Strategies.

cards.concept: Primary-Replica Replication & Failover Handling: Replication Lag & Read-Your-Own-Writes
cards.question: In a primary-replica database architecture, what consistency anomaly occurs when a user reads from a replica immediately after updating their profile?

options.text: The primary database rolls back the transaction.
Replication lag causes the read replica to return stale data (prior to the update), leading the user to believe their update was lost; mitigate by routing recent-write reads to the primary.
The database triggers an automatic primary failover.
The client connection is terminated with ECONNRESET.

cards.explanation: Asynchronous replication means replicas lag behind the primary. Read-your-own-writes consistency guarantees that a user's own updates are immediately visible to them by routing subsequent reads to the primary.
cards.pitfall: Directing all reads to read replicas without tracking mutation timestamps causes confusing UI regressions for active users.
cards.citation: Designing Data-Intensive Applications (Chapter 5: Replication)

cards.concept: Primary-Replica Replication & Failover Handling: Consistent Hashing & Sharding Key Selection
cards.question: Why is Consistent Hashing preferred over simple modulo hashing (`hash(key) % N`) when partitioning data across N database shards?

options.text: Modulo hashing requires binary database keys.
When adding or removing a shard node, modulo hashing forces almost all keys to relocate; consistent hashing remaps only K/N keys on average.
Consistent hashing compresses keys in memory.
Consistent hashing eliminates the need for primary keys.

cards.explanation: With hash(key) % N, changing N (scaling shards) redistributes almost 100% of data. Consistent hashing places nodes and keys on a logical hash ring, minimizing data movement.
cards.codeSnippet:
// Consistent hash ring maps keys to the next clockwise node
// Adding a node only reassigns keys from its direct neighbor
cards.pitfall: Selecting low-cardinality shard keys (e.g. status='ACTIVE' or date) concentrates write traffic onto a single shard hot spot.
cards.citation: Consistent Hashing and Random Trees (Karger et al.)
